simple.meaning: עַוָּל (ʻavvâl) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “evil (morally).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Job, Zephaniah, beginning at Job 18:21. Its contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַוָּל (H5767).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עַוָּל (ʻavvâl) / H5767 is traced through Job 18:21, Job 27:7, Job 29:17, Job 31:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5767. avval עַוָּל noun masculine unjust, unrighteous one ; — especially of oppressive ruler Zeph 3:5 ; Job 18:18 ; 27:7 (|| רָשָׁע ), 29:17 ; 31:3 (|| אָ֑וֶן מֹּעֲלֵי ); probably also 16:11 (for עֲוִיל ᵑ0 , so Di; || רְשָׁעִים ). I. [ עוֺלָה ] see II. עול . II. עוֺלָה see עלה . עוֺלָל עוֺלֵל, see II. עלל . עוֺלָם see עלם .
